files.why: Add "audit" to the `slices` array (and likely "audit"/"compliance" to domainNouns); single source of truth driving Oxlint/depcruise/structure tests — CODEOWNERS-protected, needs architecture review.
AuditEntry domain entity — actor, timestamp, entityType (invoice|appointment), entityId, action, field-level changes — the framework-free heart of the compliance concern.
Pure helpers to shape/group a change set into a human-readable trail (optional if the server delivers preformatted changes).
Server shape of an audit record (snake_case, ISO timestamps), kept private to data/ per the DTO rule.
Map audit DTOs to/from core AuditEntry so DTOs never leak upward.
fetchAuditTrail(entityType, entityId) — the read path compliance uses to see who/when/what.
recordAuditEntry(...) write path invoked by other slices' mutations (may be redundant if recording is purely server-side).
MSW handlers for /api/audit; where seed history and server-side append-on-change is simulated.
View state that loads an entity's audit history for display.
Reusable trail renderer (who/when/what) embedded on invoice and appointment detail pages.
Dedicated compliance log page — satisfies "Compliance needs a record" as a first-class destination and gives routes.ts a target.
Route definition for the compliance log view; required 5th slice entry.
The slice's only public surface: AuditEntry type, fetchAuditTrail, recordAuditEntry, AuditTrail component, auditRoutes, auditMockHandlers.
Compose auditMockHandlers into the MSW worker (composition-root concern).
Concatenate auditRoutes so the compliance log view is reachable.
voidInvoice must carry the actor with the request and trigger recording of the invoice change via @slices/audit (cross-slice through public index).
rescheduleAppointment must carry the actor and trigger recording of the appointment change via @slices/audit.
The void handler should append a server-side audit entry so the trail reflects the change (server is authoritative recorder).
The reschedule handler should append a server-side audit entry capturing old→new times.
Thread the current actor into voidCurrent() since the mutation now needs "who".
Thread the current actor into submit() for the same reason.
Render the AuditTrail component for the invoice so changes are visible in context.
Render the AuditTrail for the selected appointment (or AppointmentCard.vue, depending on where detail is shown).
A source of "who did it" — identity is app-wide, not domain-specific; injected at composition root. Placement uncertain.

uncertain: Whether audit should be a NEW top-level slice at all. Chose a slice because compliance/audit is a distinct reason-to-change (rule 6) and is 'about' auditing, not billing/scheduling (rule 5). But it is inherently cross-cutting, and creating it edits the CODEOWNERS-protected architecture.config.ts, forcing architecture review. The alternative — recording inline in each slice's data/mutations with no shared home — duplicates the entity and read model and is worse.

Where the current actor ('who') lives. There is currently NO user/session/auth concept anywhere in src. I put it in app/providers, but it could belong in shared/ (identity is domain-noun-free) or in a future dedicated auth slice. Biggest gap; drives several edits.

Whether client-side recordAuditEntry / data/mutations threading is correct. A compliance record must be tamper-resistant, so the authoritative recorder is the server; the frontend's real job may be only to send the actor with each mutation and display the trail. If so, audit/data/mutations.ts and client-side recording calls drop out and only the mock handlers record.
audit/core/rules.ts may be unnecessary if the API returns pre-diffed, preformatted changes; the frontend would then only render them.
Displaying the appointment trail: I guessed DayView.vue, but scheduling has no dedicated appointment-detail view — it may belong on AppointmentCard.vue or a new detail surface instead.
questions: Who is the 'actor'? Is there (or will there be) authentication / a current-user identity, or does an upstream gateway stamp identity via a header? The frontend has no user concept today, so 'who did it' has no source yet.

Is the audit trail authoritative on the server (frontend only sends the actor + displays), or is the frontend expected to construct records? Compliance normally demands server-side, append-only, tamper-evident storage.

Which changes must be captured? Only the two mutations that exist today (void invoice, reschedule appointment), or all future edits (status transitions, line-item edits, cancellations)? Determines how many mutation sites need instrumentation.
Does compliance need a global log view, per-entity trails on detail pages, or both? And do they need export (CSV/PDF) and filtering by user/date/entity, or just in-app viewing?
Any retention, immutability, granularity ('what changed' = field-level diff vs. action label), or regulatory format requirements that constrain the AuditEntry shape?
